title: The Seattle Storm Snag Jordan Horston Out Tennessee With The 9th Pick In 2023 WNBA Draft
htmlContent:
Jordan Horston's selection by the Seattle Storm with the ninth overall pick in the WNBA draft is a significant achievement and recognition of her outstanding college career. Horston, a 6-2 guard from Tennessee, has been a versatile and dynamic player for the Lady Vols, excelling in multiple positions and earning accolades for her skills on both ends of the court.

Throughout her four-year tenure at Tennessee, Horston was a consistent contributor and leader for the team, helping them to multiple NCAA Tournament appearances and establishing herself as one of the top players in the SEC. In her final season, Horston set a number of personal and program records, including becoming the second Lady Vol to record at least 1,000 points, 700 rebounds, and 400 assists in her career. She also finished seventh on the all-time career assists list at Tennessee and passed her head coach, Kellie Harper, in her final game.

Horston's selection by the Seattle Storm also adds to the impressive legacy of the Lady Vols program, which has produced 45 draft picks in WNBA history. She joins a talented roster that includes former Lady Vol Mercedes Russell, and she will have the opportunity to compete at the highest level of professional basketball while continuing to develop her game. Overall, Horston's draft selection is a testament to her hard work and dedication, and she has the potential to make a significant impact in the WNBA.
